title: Unsigned ordinary evaluation and its localization through the two augmentation comparisons
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived localization $Q$ with category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $H=R\mathcal Hom$ with its fixed K-injective augmentations $\eta_F:F\to I(F)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix the closed symmetric monoidal structure and its canonical K-flat tensor and uncurrying models [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Write $\operatorname{tr}$ for its right-tensor adjunction and $\epsilon_{L,M}:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ for its counit. Write $O=\mathcal O[0]$ and also $O$ for its derived image. For arbitrary complexes $E,F$ put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,O)$. There is a unique chain map
$$a_{E,F}:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$$
whose component on local homogeneous sections $y\in F^p$, $\phi\in D^q$, $x\in E^a$ is $a_{E,F}(y\otimes\phi)(x)=y\phi(x)$ in $F^{a+p+q}$ when $a+q=0$, and is zero when $a+q\ne0$. Here the coefficient action and the identifications with degree zero of $O$ are the actual module-sheaf action and coefficient-unit identifications. The formula fixes the map on the sheafified pure-tensor generators, total-coproduct inclusions and all Hom-product projections. Define
$$\theta_{A,B}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((B\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(A,O))\otimes^{\mathbf L}A\xrightarrow{\alpha}B\otimes^{\mathbf L}(H(A,O)\otimes^{\mathbf L}A)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{A,O}}B\otimes^{\mathbf L}O\xrightarrow{\rho}B\bigr).$$
Suppose $F,D$ are K-flat, and the maps $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_O)$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_F)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Let $\gamma_{E,G}:Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(QE,QG)$, for $G=O,F$, be induced by those augmentations and the fixed derived-Hom comparisons. Let $\mu:Q\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF\otimes^{\mathbf L}QD$ be the canonical K-flat tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Then
$$\theta_{QE,QF}\circ(1\otimes\gamma_{E,O})\circ\mu=\gamma_{E,F}\circ Q(a_{E,F}).$$
In particular the ordinary formula has no Koszul sign. No K-flatness of $E$ or K-injectivity of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the proved chain-level right-tensor currying equivalence and its generator and naturality formulas from the ringed derived tensor-Hom adjunction construction. It compares the ordinary Hom complex with the native internal Hom complex and applies complex symmetry; the two Koszul signs cancel, so its formula on pure sections is unsigned. This supplies an actual chain equivalence for arbitrary complexes, before localization.

proof.text: Define a_E,F by right-tensor currying of ordinary reassociation, F tensor ordinary evaluation into O[0], and the ordinary right unitor. These are chain maps, so the construction needs no new differential calculation. The pure-section formulas for the constraints give y φ(x) in the supported component a+q=0; O[0] vanishes in every other component. Hom product projections, total coproduct inclusions and the sheafification adjunction detect equality and prove uniqueness. Applying the same detection twice identifies the ordinary associator and right unitor with the representatives in the supplied coherence.

proof.text: The fixed localization factorization is a natural isomorphism on pairs of complexes. Its naturality and naturality of the fixed K-injective augmentation imply Q Hom(s,G) followed by γ_L,G equals γ_E,G followed by H(Qs,1). Each assumed augmentation quasi-isomorphism gives invertibility of its own γ. No general preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by Hom(E,-) is used.

source.place: Tag 08JD (lemma-dual), equation-eval (Tag 08JE), Tag 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), and section-hom-complexes; ordinary chain map and its fixed-augmentation derived comparison.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution s:L→E. Put D=Hom(E,O), P=Tot(F tensor D), and v equal to the ordinary uncurrying of Hom(s,O). The tensor of K-flat complexes is K-flat. Apply the fixed coefficient tensor-curry normalization to (D,L) and (P,L). It identifies the inverse transpose of γ_E,O followed by H(Qs,1) with μ_D,L inverse followed by Qv; similarly the other inverse transpose is μ_P,L inverse followed by Qc, where c is the uncurrying of a followed by Hom(s,F). Naturality of ordinary uncurrying and of the ordinary associator identifies c with reassociation, F tensor v and the right unitor.

source.place: Tag 08JD (lemma-dual), equation-eval (Tag 08JE), Tag 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), and section-hom-complexes; ordinary chain map and its fixed-augmentation derived comparison.

proof.text: Compute the inverse transpose of the left side of the desired square after postcomposition with H(Qs,1). Naturality of the adjunction in both inputs expresses it as the derived associator, tensor with the normalized inverse transpose from the preceding step, and the unit constraint. The supplied associator model, tensorIso naturality on v and right-unitor model turn this into μ_P,L inverse followed by Qc. For tensor with O only the one-K-flat comparison is needed. Injectivity of inverse transposition proves equality after H(Qs,1); cancel this isomorphism because Qs is invertible. Combine this equality with the two γ invertibility conclusions and the ordinary existence and uniqueness.
